key_insight: Generative LLMs can evaluate ASR outputs in a meaning-aware way—using pairwise selection, generative embeddings, and qualitative LLM judgments—providing signals better aligned with human perception than raw WER.
problem_solved: Standard WER is insensitive to meaning and can misrepresent perceived transcription quality; decoder-based LLMs as evaluators have been underexplored for producing semantic-aware ASR evaluation.
method: Pairwise selection: use an LLM to choose the better hypothesis between two ASR outputs.
Generative embeddings: extract embeddings from a generative LLM to compute semantic distance between reference and hypothesis.
Qualitative LLM analysis: use generative LLM outputs for classification/qualitative assessment of error types and semantic deviations.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with evaluation tools that reflect semantic fidelity and human judgment, enabling more meaningful benchmarking and model selection beyond WER. This can guide development toward systems that preserve intended meaning rather than just token-level accuracy.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison diagram of WER vs. LLM-based evaluation showing different outcomes for the same ASR outputs
Bar/line chart of correlation with human judgments: WER vs. embedding-based vs. LLM pairwise scoring

paper_title: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
paper_authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek
